label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, secret-rotation, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 6 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy webhook-receiver: WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION v2 -> v1); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.name: secret-rotation
case.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook
case.right_answer: The fault's recorded cause: a deploy of the webhook receiver with a rotated secret the provider does not sign with (WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, while the provider signs with v1): every webhook fails its signature check and is refused with a 400, so no event reaches Kafka, and the provider keeps sending them again, with backoff.
case.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

fault.title: The books stop catching up: our webhook receiver refuses every webhook

expected_symptoms: the books cannot catch up with the provider: the money check cannot settle, the provider's webhooks not acknowledged, and the books rule fires at its second evaluation, about 50 s after the deploy
the receiver refuses every webhook with a 400, counts it as bad_signature and logs 'webhook refused: bad signature'; the provider sends its growing backlog again and again, tens of times a second
nothing new is booked or confirmed, and both consumers' lag stays at 0: nothing reaches Kafka

payments and refunds still go through, but one whose answer was lost cannot be confirmed: its client's retries get 503 again, so the 5xx share of POST /payments about doubles and its p95 climbs to about 0.6 s, both under their thresholds

after the rollback the books catch up within about three minutes: the provider sends each refused webhook again within a minute of its last try, and one whose acknowledgement is then lost (the traffic's noise) a minute later
fault.remedy: roll the webhook receiver back to v1 (or accept both versions until the provider signs with v2): the provider sends every refused webhook again, and the books catch up by themselves

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, 131 of the provider's webhooks up to it had not been acknowledged yet.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 07:59:04 webhook-receiver was redeployed with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. The provider still signs its webhooks with the previous secret, so the receiver now fails the signature check on every webhook. It replies with a rejection instead of an acknowledgement and never puts the event on provider-events. The provider retries each unacknowledged webhook, and each retry is rejected again. So the received rate climbs, nothing reaches ledger-consumer or payment-confirmer, and the money check cannot settle: 131 webhooks were unacknowledged at the last evaluation. The evidence does not show which secret version the provider uses, or whether the v2 secret is wrong or just not yet rotated on the provider's side. Either way, the receiver and the provider now disagree on the secret. The receiver logged nothing at WARN or ERROR for these rejections, so they show only in the metric.

evidence.shows: webhook-receiver was recreated at 07:59:04Z with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2, the latest deploy, about a minute before the alert at 07:59:52Z. The other services were last deployed at 07:57:38Z.

Before the deploy all webhooks were result=queued (about 3.9/s at 07:59:01). From 07:59:21 result=bad_signature appears and grows to 19.3/s by 08:00:21, while queued falls to 0.9/s and then stops reporting. Every webhook is now rejected.
The total webhook rate rose from about 4/s to 18.8/s after the deploy, which fits the provider retrying rejected, unacknowledged webhooks.
The receiver logged no WARN or ERROR lines in the last 10 minutes, so the signature rejections are not logged at those levels.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll webhook-receiver back to its settings before the 07:59:04 deploy, so it uses the previous webhook secret version the provider still signs with. The provider's retries should then be accepted and queued, and the consumers can catch up. Afterwards, check that klaxon_webhooks_received_total{result="bad_signature"} drops to zero, then run money_check. Re-attempt the v2 rotation only once the provider signs with v2, or once the receiver accepts both versions.

diagnosis.blast_radius: webhook-receiver pauses while its container is recreated. The provider keeps retrying meanwhile, so no webhooks should be lost. After the rollback a burst of retried webhooks will be queued, and the consumers face a short spike in load and lag. Duplicate deliveries are possible, but the consumers run idempotent and by_our_id handlers. If the v2 rotation was needed for security, rolling back keeps the old secret in use for longer.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy webhook-receiver with WEBHOOK_SECRET_VERSION=v2. Make sure the provider signs with v2 first, or the same rejections will return.
